findings.where: First screen, Mark's portrait set flush in the right half of the paper frame (desktop); the same photo inset under the nav on phone
findings.fault: The portrait's studio backdrop stays a cool, flat grey and fills nearly half of the first screen. It meets the warm ivory paper along a hard vertical edge, so the hero looks like two surfaces pasted together, not one sheet of paper. The tile's own palette note says the photographs are multiplied onto the paper so their light backdrops take its warmth. The render shows that hasn't happened.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who judges the first screen first and asked for one soft ground with imagery graded into the house colours. The cold grey slab next to the warm paper is the first thing a visitor's eye meets, and it undercuts the 'one sheet of Counsel's paper' idea that this direction rests on.

findings.where: Article specimen, the lectern photograph under the opening paragraphs
findings.fault: Turning the photo to greyscale makes the purple stage backdrop a large near-solid charcoal block, almost the logo grey. This is by far the darkest and heaviest surface anywhere on the light, quiet page. It outweighs the article's heading and turns 'grey is ink' into a dark field. It is also a second photo treatment (greyscale here, colour in the hero) for the same subject on the same site.
findings.who_objects: A reader at a development bank opening one of Mark's articles, whose eye is pulled to a dark slab instead of the text. Mark, too, who is shown against what reads as a black backdrop on a page meant to feel like a light legal journal.

findings.where: First screen, the hairline frame round the whole sheet (desktop and phone); the same line on the texture specimen
findings.fault: The frame meant as a paper's edge is drawn in the full text grey. It reads as a crisp ink outline, like a box drawn round the page, not the soft edge of a sheet. It is as dark as the body text, so it competes with the words in a ground the brief wants quiet and low in contrast.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who asked for legal-pad borders to be placed with careful intention and the ground kept quiet. A full-ink box round the first screen edges towards the 'sheet frame' look that round 1 was told to avoid.

findings.where: Phone first screen, the pad-yellow 'Write to me directly' band
findings.fault: On phone, the yellow band sits between the headline and the supporting paragraph, with paper continuing below it inside the frame. The one colour memory then cuts the sheet in two mid-way, instead of sitting at its foot as on desktop and as the tile itself describes ('only at the foot of the sheet'). The pad yellow takes a different role at each width.
findings.who_objects: A phone visitor, who sees a coloured band split the hero and may take the paragraph below it for a separate section. The founder, too, because the yellow's one intended meaning (the sender's address at the foot of a letter) is lost on the width most first visits use.
